description:
Roughly 1 cluster start in 50, with NO faults injected, comes up with one node that publishes no layout and can never transact. It does not recover -- a probe retried 12 times over 60s never succeeded.

Captured state from a wedged 3-node cluster (bedrock-hve.5 harness dumps this on readiness timeout):

    c1: layout epoch=2 ...                 coordinator #PID<27104.190.0>   commit probe: :ok
    c2: layout {:error, :unavailable}      coordinator #PID<27105.191.0>   commit probe: :unavailable
    c3: layout epoch=2 ...                 coordinator #PID<27104.190.0>   commit probe: :ok

c1 and c3 agree on the leader's coordinator pid. c2 holds ITS OWN coordinator pid. Because it never learns the transaction system layout, it can never commit or read, and nothing repairs it. The other two nodes are perfectly healthy, so the cluster looks fine from outside -- this is a partial, silent failure, not an outage.

It follows a leadership flap during formation: logs show 'Received :undecided leadership change' and an epoch 1 -> 2 transition before the node gets stuck.

Two open tickets look related and may share a root cause -- worth checking before designing a fix:
- bedrock-ued: a stale nil tsl_updated from an abandoned leader can blank the cached layout until the current leader's next broadcast
- bedrock-ltc: a :passive Link never registers node resources, so it is never in tsl_subscribers and its TSL cache stays nil

The 'until the next broadcast' in bedrock-ued is suspicious given this node never recovers: if a node misses the broadcast and nothing re-broadcasts or re-subscribes, 'until the next broadcast' is 'forever'.

## Provenance and confidence

Found by bedrock-hve.5, the deliberately fault-free chaos baseline, across ~165 cluster starts (~3 occurrences, ~2%). The agent that found it explicitly declined to add formation retries that would have masked it.

NOT yet independently reproduced -- I ran 10 cluster starts and saw 0 occurrences, which is consistent with a 2% rate but confirms nothing. The evidence is the captured diagnostic above rather than a reproduction on demand. Anyone picking this up should first build a tight start/stop loop to get the sample size up, since the full workload test is a slow way to sample cluster formation.

Impact on the chaos harness: this is the failure mode the epic exists to find, discovered before any fault injection was even built. It also means the harness cannot yet distinguish 'my fault injection broke the cluster' from 'the cluster was born broken' unless readiness is strict -- which is why bedrock-hve.5's readiness gate now requires a real committed transaction on every node rather than trusting a published layout.

comments.text:
Very likely the same root cause as bedrock-5yi, found independently from the other direction. Whoever picks up either should read both first.

bedrock-5yi observation 3: 'One :undecided leadership change fired on all three nodes at once with every node healthy and idle, ~66s after boot... That election handed leadership to a follower with a stale prior_core_state and wiped the cluster.'

This ticket: a node stuck holding its own coordinator pid while its peers hold the leader's, never learning the layout, never serving -- immediately following an :undecided leadership change and an epoch 1 -> 2 transition, with no faults injected.

Same trigger (a spurious :undecided election among healthy nodes), different observed consequence. 5yi documents the flap; this documents one node's permanent end state afterward. A fix for the election instability may well close both, and a repro for either is probably a repro for the other.

Also relevant: 5yi notes elections are LOAD-DEPENDENT -- 'quiet machine hides them'. That fits the reproduction rate here. This was found by the chaos baseline (bedrock-hve.5) running 6 concurrent workers against a 3-node cluster, i.e. under load, at ~2% of cluster starts. A harness that drives real load may be a more reliable reproducer than an idle cluster, which is worth knowing before anyone tries to build a deterministic repro.

Independent reproduction context: ../bedrock_ex has a live 3-node harness (three_node.sh / load.sh / storm_ab.sh, BURN=24 for CPU pressure) built for exactly this class of bug.

title: [BUG] A node can permanently believe the wrong coordinator after a formation leadership flap, and never serves
